question: Two first knots of three to six places, apart or sharing one or two distinctions, and small starts of several knots, grown by the cubic study's joining rule under one count and under the fewest counts: which counts run, what grows, and does anything prefer the smallest knot?

definitions.Lemma 1 scope: no two start knots have a common neighbour
definitions.relay: a top's single fresh distinction equal to a start-shared distinction on every allowed state

public_inputs.reused: freelib.py of FRESH-COUNT-20261118-001B (closed record), imported by path

forbidden_inputs: Changing cases, rules, predictions or decision rules after seeing registered results
primary_observable: G and Q1-Q5 of research/FIRST-KNOT-20261118-001/preregistration.md, scored by merge.py.
cheapest_meaningful_control: checks.py gates (one-knot replay, GF(2) closure, pieces never mix, refusal, two N^3) and the floor control Q5.

predictions.Q1: one count runs iff every start knot has l in {0,1,c}; stall round min r(l,c); counts as predicted (scored in Lemma 1's scope)
predictions.Q2: fewest: apart closes as two Boolean patterns; sharing one grows two N^2 with exact per-round counts and one relay per piece with l >= 3
predictions.Q4: small starts and two-distinction touches under fewest: closed iff every demand-0 junction implied; else constant differences over the last ten rounds; no forced distinction
predictions.Q5: floor 2: constant per-round counts; floor 4: strictly increasing differences

decision_rules.each prediction: holds or fails as scored by merge.py

stop_rule: One run; read-out; proofs; referee hand-off; report.
runtime: 7 workers through scripts/longrun.py, a few minutes
